newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso strong.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso strong.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen mixed to down on Cetes hike
--Peso likely strong on U.S. long bond, Cetes rates
--Overnight Cetes rate viewed down on U.S. data
Traders saw stocks opening mixed to down on Wednesday in quiet trade as the market assimilated conflicting news.
Share prices were seen benefitting from a buoyant Dow Jones in the wake of mild producer price data, but would also be weighed down by hikes in primary local rates late Tuesday.
"It should be quiet and down a little, we only closed up because of window-dressing yesterday," one desk trader said.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 18.91 percent at Tuesday night's auction, an increase of 54 basis points since last week, compared to a rise of 76 basis points forecast in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
Traders expected the peso to open strong on a stable U.S. bond market and gains in domestic Cetes rates. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 15/32 to yield 6.89 percent in early trade.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.8800/7.9000 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso.
Pre-open bids stood at 7.8900/7.8950 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.9060/7.9090.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen edging down from Tuesday's close of 19.25 percent.
